title: BeeZip: Towards An Organized and Scalable Architecture for Data Compression
problem: Data compression has become CPU-intensive due to extensive hash table manipulation and matching operations on large data volumes. Prior hardware accelerators (using CAM, redundant historical copies) improve throughput but sacrifice compression ratio and consume excessive memory when scaling to large sliding window algorithms.
motivation: Data compression is critical for reducing network bandwidth consumption and memory/storage capacity utilization in operating systems and large-scale computing.
method: BeeZip proposes an organized and scalable architecture that addresses the throughput-compression ratio trade-off of prior hardware accelerators. The design aims to maintain better compression ratios while achieving performance improvements and reducing memory resource costs in large sliding window implementations.
key_novelty: Scalable compression architecture that preserves compression ratio while enabling hardware acceleration without proportional memory overhead.
contributions: Organized architecture balancing compression throughput and compression ratio
Memory-efficient handling of large sliding window algorithms
Scalable design for hardware-accelerated data compression
limitations: Specific performance metrics and experimental evaluation not discussed in abstract.
